messages:
maya (eng-platform): Heads-up — product asked for a runtime dashboard for model-serving telemetry (latency, queue depth, cache hit, model fallback counts). We need alert rules and pager routing before we flip canary. Who owns what?
kevin (eng-runtime): I can own the instrumentation side. Metric names I plan to expose: runtime_request_latency_ms{model,region}, runtime_queue_length, kv_cache_hit_ratio, model_fallback_count. Note: p99 is expensive to compute for high-cardinality labels; plan to approximate with quantiles + aggregation.
jordan (eng-sre): Thanks — for paging we'll want two levels: P1 (hard SLO burn / outage) and P2 (degradation). My suggested alert signatures:
- P1: slo_burn_rate{team="runtime"} > 4 for 5m
- P2: increase(model_fallback_count[5m]) > 20 OR runtime_queue_length > 200 for 5m
sam (eng-ml): Model-level context matters. fallback_count should be broken down by model_version and route. If a single model spikes fallback we may degrade to a lighter model; want automatic on-call hints to include recent commits and rollout id.
lia (product): UX note — for canary rollouts we want a non-paging alert that posts to #canary-watch and the rollout UI; only escalate to pager if P1. Also want a short blurb in the alert showing affected percentage of traffic.
maya (eng-platform): Agree. Routing idea: P1 -> eng-oncall (pager) + infra-rotation; P2 -> #canary-watch + eng-platform-ops (no immediate pager). Jordan, can you map to paging groups?
jordan (eng-sre): Proposed mapping:
- slo_burn_rate P1 -> page eng-oncall (rotation: infra + runtime on-call)
- fallback_count P2 -> notify eng-platform, post to #canary-watch
- fallback_count P1 (if > 100 in 5m across cluster) -> page runtime on-call
Also suggest a 10m suppression window after automated rollback to avoid noise.
kevin (eng-runtime): For thresholds: p99 latency > 1200ms for >5m = P2; p99 > 3000ms = P1. kv_cache_hit_ratio drop > 15% relative to baseline = P2. Baseline computed over 1h rolling window.
sam (eng-ml): Add model-quality guardrail: if rouge/bleu-like eval deltas (from canary eval job) degrade beyond threshold, trigger P2. Those evals run post-deploy and feed telemetry.
maya (eng-platform): Ops concern: quotas. If big spike causes shared quota exhaustion we need soft-fail alerts earlier. Suggest adding "quota_pressure" metric: quota_utilization > 90% -> paged to capacity team (P1 if >95% for 3m).
jordan (eng-sre): Agree. For SLO burn alerts, use burn-rate so we avoid paging on transient blips. Burn-rate thresholds: 5m burn > 3 -> warn (P2), > 8 -> page (P1). We'll tie it to incident runbooks.
lia (product): Can we include the rollout id and canary cohort size in the alert payload? That will speed debugging.
kevin (eng-runtime): Yes — we'll enrich metrics with labels rollout_id and cohort_pct where available. May increase cardinality; we will cap it to canary-only labels to avoid cardinal explosion.
maya (eng-platform): Action items:
- kevin: instrument quota_pressure + rollout labels (ETA Tue EOD)
- jordan: draft alert expressions and pager mapping + runbook links (ETA Wed noon)
- sam: hook canary eval job to telemetry stream for quality alerts (ETA Wed EOD)
- lia: update rollout UX to show alert link and canary cohort (ETA Fri)
- maya: validate dashboards and make sure panels include quick link to runbooks (ETA Thu)
jordan (eng-sre): I'll also add a temporary silence policy for automatic rollbacks (10m). We should later revisit silence heuristics.
oncall-bot: deploy 1748954300 by kevin to prod/runtime-metrics - instrumented metrics: runtime_queue_length, kv_cache_hit_ratio, rollback_signal
kevin (eng-runtime): Deployed to canary. Please verify metrics show up in prometheus/metrics explorer. Query examples:
```
avg_over_time(runtime_request_latency_ms{job="runtime",quantile="0.99"}[5m])
increase(model_fallback_count{rollout_id!=""}[5m])
```
maya (eng-platform): I'll check dashboards now and start wiring alerts. If anyone wants different thresholds, call them out here within 6 hours or I'll proceed with Jordan's numbers.
sam (eng-ml): Quick ask: include model_version label on fallback_count for first pass. If cardinality is a problem, we'll fallback to sampling.
kevin (eng-runtime): Added model_version label in canary. If we hit cardinality issues we'll switch to sampled counter.
maya (eng-platform): Perfect — moving to implement. We'll post PRs for alerting config and ownership docs when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:
